clue.text: I take turns, moving from Central Asian region

indicators.note: the letters are moving about, so the words I take turns are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes taking turns at the wheel while travelling out of a remote stretch of Central Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes turns' reads like the action of a traveller; the whole phrase 'I take turns' is the fodder for 'moving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkestan is the historical name for the broad Central Asian territory, so its adjective describes that region.

clue.text: Treaty wrapped up in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing tells us the word is only heard, so we enter what sounds the same

parts.note: wrapped up means packed, as goods in a parcel

explanation.surface: An agreement is settled and sealed during a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hearing' looks like a courtroom, but it signals that PACKED is spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement between parties, the same thing as a treaty between states.

clue.text: Joker returns in the flesh, initially tasting a lot of power

indicators.note: in places the turned joker inside the word for flesh

parts.note: flesh as food is meat

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for the joker comes back the other way

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of tasting

explanation.surface: A comedian comes back in person, having tasted great power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the flesh' reads as the idiom for 'in person', so solvers miss that 'in' is doing the insertion on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A megawatt is a million watts, a large unit of electrical output.

clue.text: Doctor returning British papers relating to disease

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: returning tells us the abbreviation for British is turned back

parts.note: ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A doctor brings back British documents about an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is the usual crossword doctor; 'returning' acts only on British, not on the whole run of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbid is a medical term for anything pertaining to or caused by illness, as in morbid anatomy.

clue.text: Lounge's length tripled to hold a ball?

indicators.note: to hold means the three letters wrap around the ball

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for length, written three times
a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A question of whether a sitting room three times longer would fit a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' looks like a dance in a long lounge; it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to sprawl or recline lazily, which is a verb sense of lounge.

clue.text: Distressed, reinstated after a fashion

indicators.note: after a fashion means done in some rough manner, so the letters of reinstated are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone upset at being only partly restored to their old job.
explanation.definitionFit: Straitened circumstances are hard-up ones; distressed here means financially pressed or troubled.

clue.text: Old killer maintains right of returning, in case

indicators.note: maintains means the disease holds the other letters within it

parts.note: polio was once a widespread fatal disease, now largely eradicated

indicators.note: returning tells us the little word of is written backwards

explanation.surface: A former murderer keeps his rights in returning to court for his case.
explanation.walkthrough: Polio is the 'old killer' because vaccination has made it rare; 'returning' reverses only the little word 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for papers or drawings.

clue.text: Youngster turns to sink, not wrong to spit

indicators.note: not means the word for wrong is left out

parts.note: taken as written
a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: turns to means the youngster is turned round and comes next

parts.note: a babe is a baby, a youngster

explanation.surface: A child turning to the kitchen sink is told it is not wrong to spit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns to' both reverses the youngster and sends it on to the reduced sink, so the sink's letter comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is meat cooked on a skewer, and the word is also used for the skewer, a spit, itself.

clue.text: Splendour of city almost dead

parts.note: EC is the postcode district for the City of London

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for dead is cut off

parts.note: the late king is the dead king

explanation.surface: The glory of a city that has very nearly died.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the City of London's postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliance of display or effect, a borrowed French word for showy splendour.

clue.text: One prosecuting wickedness arrests left-wing desperado

indicators.note: arrests means the outer letters seize and hold the left-wing word

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, the American public prosecutor
evil is wickedness
red is a byword for left-wing politics

explanation.surface: A prosecutor pursues the crimes of a radical outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: DA, the district attorney, is an American prosecutor; red as left-wing comes from the colour of socialist flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a recklessly bold person, and a desperado is someone reckless and ready for anything.

clue.text: Natural to tour county, rambling

indicators.note: to tour means to go all the way round, so the word for natural surrounds county

parts.note: inherent means natural, built-in

explanation.surface: It is only natural to go round a county on a long walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' suggests walking in the country, but it means disjointed speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoherent talk is disconnected and confused, like a rambling speech that wanders without sense.

clue.text: One fixing the pitch shortening a fissure

indicators.note: shortening means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a cleft is a crack or fissure

explanation.surface: A groundsman repairing the cricket pitch by narrowing a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field; it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef at the start of a stave sets which notes the lines stand for, fixing their musical pitch.

clue.text: Centre of activity features extravagant outdoor amenity

indicators.note: features means the hub contains the other piece

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity
OTT is short for over the top, extravagant

explanation.surface: A busy resort hub boasts a lavish outdoor facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a heated outdoor bath for soaking, a garden or hotel facility.

clue.text: Drawing back from golf after business with Ireland

indicators.note: after places golf at the end, following the rest

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
G is golf in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone withdrawing from golf after a business deal in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing back from golf' reads as one phrase; 'from' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowering is shrinking or recoiling in fear, the same as drawing back.

clue.text: Not entirely sane Roman?

indicators.note: not entirely means the answer is part of the following words, not all of them

explanation.surface: Asks whether a certain Roman was quite in his right mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: the emperor hides in the words, and the clue describes him, a Roman widely thought unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor whose cruelty and erratic rule earned a reputation for madness.

clue.text: Bearing right, soldiers enter headquarters

indicators.note: enter means these pieces go inside the word for headquarters

parts.note: a depot is a regimental headquarters
soldiers are men

explanation.surface: Troops march into base, bearing right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing right' reads as a direction; 'Bearing' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is the way a person carries themselves, their posture and manner.

clue.text: Sort of photographing simple tea being cooked

indicators.note: being cooked means the letters are worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Filming a plain afternoon meal as it is prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography takes frames at intervals and plays them fast to show slow change.

clue.text: Soldier takes up artillery weapon

indicators.note: takes up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A soldier picks up a big gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional full-time soldier, as opposed to a reservist.

clue.text: Picture of bridges being erected very popular

indicators.note: being erected in a down clue means the word is built upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a bridge spans a gap, so bridges means spans
something hot is very popular, in demand

explanation.surface: A photo of bridges going up, a hit with everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly, a type of picture.

clue.text: Amputation scare turned out an exaggerated fuss

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fears of losing a limb proved to be overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' reads as 'proved to be', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes great anger or worry over a trivial matter, an overblown commotion.

clue.text: One's a writer of certain lines of verse

parts.note: one's is read as I'm, short for I am
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be a poet of a particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: One's = I'm = I am, the speaker declaring themself; BIC is a pen brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic describes metre built of iambs, a short then long syllable, as in much English poetry.

clue.text: Don't surrender chop new peer needs to eat

indicators.note: needs to eat means the reworked peer swallows the other word
new means the letters of peer are made fresh, rearranged

parts.note: to chop is to sever

explanation.surface: A newly ennobled peer must keep eating chops without giving up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns PEER into PERE, which then eats SEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist despite difficulty, carrying on rather than giving in.

clue.text: Fancy smartphone feature: welcome as replacement for earlier article

indicators.note: as replacement for means the greeting takes the place of the article

parts.note: a camera is a standard feature of a smartphone
A is the indefinite article; earlier means the first of the two A's
hi is a greeting, a welcome

explanation.surface: A fancy smartphone screen welcomes the user as a replacement for an old model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the phone; it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful illusion or wild imagining, so a fancy in the sense of a fantasy.

clue.text: What hotel may offer for very few people, or a number

definitions.text: What hotel may offer for very few people
definitions.meaning: first meaning: tea served for a couple of guests
second meaning: a song, the jazz standard from No, No, Nanette

explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count of guests, but it is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a hotel serving for a pair and the title of a famous popular song.

clue.text: Contest where result of the toss could be fatal

definitions.text: Contest where result of the toss could be fatal

parts.words: Contest where result of the toss could be fatal
parts.note: the toss sounds like a coin toss before a match, but here a matador may be tossed on horns

explanation.walkthrough: A coin toss starts a sporting contest harmlessly; in this contest the toss is by an animal's horns.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bullfight the matador risks being gored or thrown by the animal, which can kill.

clue.text: Abbeys regularly keep one donating

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Monasteries routinely retain a benefactor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestower is someone who gives or confers something, a giver.

clue.text: Forgive scam, being tricked

parts.note: a con is a scam
done means cheated, tricked

explanation.surface: Pardoning a fraud after being duped.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or excuse an offence, accepting it without punishment.

clue.text: Liven up foolish cunning

indicators.note: foolish means the letters are mixed up in a silly way

explanation.surface: Brighten up a dull and sly fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulpine means fox-like, and the fox is proverbially crafty, so the word also means crafty.

clue.text: Ready to sleep, but first sponge extremely wet floor

indicators.note: first places those end letters before the rest
extremely means only the extreme letters of sponge are used

parts.note: outer letters of sponge
abed means in bed, settled for sleep

explanation.surface: Someone about to go to bed must first mop up a soaking floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet floor' sounds like housework; it is the floor of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabed lies under water at the bottom of the ocean, so it is a floor that is always soaked.
